Keyboard shortcut tool TextExpander launches a free plan, allowing users to use its core Snippets feature on Mac, iPhone, iPad, Windows and Chrome. Details as follows.

TextExpander Launches Free Plan

I have previously introduced TextExpander — it's one of the applications I install every time I switch to a new Mac.

Over the years, I have built up about 200 Snippets (TextExpander calls text abbreviations that can be automatically expanded into preset text "Snippets"), most of which I use frequently, such as quickly replying to emails, filling out forms, preparing podcast outlines, reading out sponsor names, writing show notes, etc.

Although macOS's built-in text replacement feature continues to improve, features like filling in variables, conditional paragraphs, nested Snippets, and math macros still make TextExpander an indispensable tool for me.

TextExpander recently launched a free plan. According to the company to 9to5Mac, the plan offers 5 active Snippets, unlimited storage, unlimited text expansions, and up to 5 team members. The free plan also supports Mac, iPhone, iPad, Windows, and Chrome, syncing the same Snippet library across devices.

The 5 Snippet limit is undoubtedly a bit restrictive, especially since the free plan only allows swapping one active Snippet every two weeks.

However, this can also be a good way to gradually adopt TextExpander — leaving shorter, simpler text replacements to macOS, and saving this application for longer or more complex Snippets.

To learn more about TextExpander's free plan, please follow this link.
